timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So how does networking work in Zero Trust? No more firewalls?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Firewalls still exist. But the idea of a trusted internal network is gone.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What does that mean exactly? I'm inside the building, I should be trusted!

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Microsegmentation splits your network into tiny isolated zones.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So if an attacker gets in one zone, they can't reach the others?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Exactly. Each zone has its own rules. No free lateral movement.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: What about web apps? Those seem like easy targets.

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Azure Web Application Firewall inspects and blocks malicious web traffic.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: And how do admins securely access servers for maintenance?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Azure Bastion. It's a hardened jump box. No public RDP or SSH needed.

timeline.speaker: Peter
timeline.text: So the old DMZ concept is just... dead?

timeline.speaker: Stewie
timeline.text: Dead and buried. In Zero Trust, every network segment is treated as hostile.
